subject: Request: rollback flag & staggered purge for Medigen legal hold
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@medigen.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Medigen Legal <legal@medigen.com>
Date: 2026-12-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Urgent: Delay to scheduled backups purge / legal hold

Hi Kimberly,

We received notice that Redwood has a scheduled purge of historical backups and offsite snapshots for our tenant next week. Medigen has just opened an internal investigation related to a clinical data ingestion incident and Legal has issued an immediate legal hold on a subset of records.

Can you please:
- Pause any automated purge for the Medigen tenant until we confirm scope (we expect 72 hours to narrow scope).
- Provide an audit-friendly statement of your deletion workflow (how snapshot TTLs are applied and how a purge runs).
- Confirm whether Redwood can mark affected snapshots with an "escrow" flag that prevents purge (or provide an alternate safe-guard).

I've attached the legal hold notice. We understand this is tight; please confirm next steps and an ETA.

Thanks,
Ellen Park
Sr. Legal Counsel
Medigen Solutions

Attachment: medigen_legal_hold_notice.pdf (application/pdf, 78KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Ellen Park <ellen.park@medigen.com>
Date: 2026-12-18T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: Delay to scheduled backups purge / legal hold

Ellen — received, and thanks for the heads up.

Marissa / Karthik — looping you both in to triage. Key asks from Medigen: pause next-week purge for their tenant, provide deletion workflow documentation, and a mechanism to tag snapshots so they are skipped by the purge. They expect a 72-hour window to scope; Legal copied here.

High-level proposal (we can refine):
- Hold: apply a tenant-level "rollback_token" boolean on Medigen's retention index to prevent automated purge jobs from selecting those snapshots.
- Stagger: for non-impacted customers, keep the normal purge cadence; for Medigen do a withheld stage (no destructive actions) until Legal confirms scope.
- Evidence: provide a short runbook + exportable audit log (timestamps, snapshot ids, operator id).

Questions for Ops/legal:
1) Can we implement the rollback_token within the next 6 hours as a short-term guard?
2) Are there any subprocessor or cross-border transfer implications if we freeze snapshots longer (Medigen is EU-headquartered)?
3) Karthik — once Medigen confirms scope, do we need a signed DPA addendum or is an email hold sufficient to block purge?

Marissa — can you draft the purge phasing matrix and a command checklist (attachment to share with Medigen)? Karthik — please confirm DPA path and whether we should prepare a temporary restriction of transfers while under hold.

Kimberly Park
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Ellen Park <ellen.park@medigen.com>
Date: 2026-12-18T13:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: Delay to scheduled backups purge / legal hold

On Fri, Dec 18, 2026 at 10:03 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com> wrote:
> Ellen — received, and thanks for the heads up.
> 
> Marissa / Karthik — looping you both in to triage. Key asks from Medigen: pause next-week purge for their tenant, provide deletion workflow documentation, and a mechanism to tag snapshots so they are skipped by the purge. They expect a 72-hour window to scope; Legal copied here.

Thanks Kim — quick ops note below and a tentative implementation plan. I attached the matrix and a short spec for the rollback token.

Summary of operational controls we can apply immediately:
- rollback_token flag: boolean on tenant metadata. Purge goroutines check this flag at selection time; if true, snapshots are excluded. Can be set via admin console or API. Estimated turnaround: 2 hours to apply and propagate to all purge workers.
- snapshot retention index freeze: mark all snapshot rows for tenant with freeze=true; purge job will skip rows with freeze tag. Adds zero-downtime overhead.
- staged purge window: we can move Medigen's next scheduled purge out by 14 days or until Legal sends final scope (internal default is 7 days but we can extend).

Operational checklist (short):
1) Create rollback_token on tenant: POST /admin/tenants/{id}/flags {rollback_token:true}
2) Verify propagation: GET /admin/purge-workers/status -> ensure worker list shows tenant exclusion (expected 2-10 min propagation).
3) Run a dry-run report: admin job -> /admin/purge/dryrun?tenant=medigen -> export CSV of snapshot ids that would have been deleted. Share with Medigen for verification.
4) Audit export: admin -> /admin/audit/export?tenant=medigen&range=2026-06-01_2026-12-18 -> signed export.

Notes on backups/retention internals:
- Offsite snapshots are stored with a tombstone TTL; physical deletion is deferred until secondary confirmation job runs (this is the job we'll pause).
- If we implement rollback_token, it prevents the confirmation job from marking snapshots for physical deletion; it does not revert already-compact snapshots.

Attachments included for Medigen: purge_phasing_matrix.xlsx (tabbed view of phases and operators), rollback_token_spec.md (fields/protocol).

I'll plan to run step 1 immediately after Kimberly confirms.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Manager, Technical Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: purge_phasing_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 24KB); rollback_token_spec.md (text, 6KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ellen Park <ellen.park@medigen.com>
Date: 2026-12-18T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: Delay to scheduled backups purge / legal hold

Kimberly / Marissa — good plan. A few legal/compliance items to add before we confirm with Medigen: 

1) DPA addendum vs. email hold:
- An email hold from Medigen Legal is sufficient to implement a short-term operational pause. For anything longer than 30 days or where the hold affects cross-border transfers, we should have a signed DPA addendum that references the hold/escrow controls.

2) Subprocessors / transfers: 
- We need to check the current subprocessors that may hold copies (offsite archival provider and the cloud region replicator). I'll run a quick subprocessor hit-list. If any storage subprocessor is in a non-EEA jurisdiction, we should suspend cross-border replication for the Medigen tenant until Legal confirms.

3) Evidence for audit / SOC2:
- Prepare a single combined package: (a) purge dry-run CSV, (b) audit export, (c) signed admin change log (who set rollback_token and when). That is what auditors will want.

4) DocuSign / DPA workflow:
- I'll create a DPA addendum template and send via DocuSign with conditional language that references the rollback_token and retention freeze. Link to sample clause included in the drive.

Action items:
- Marissa: apply rollback_token and run dry-run report; share CSV with Medigen.
- Me: freeze replication to any non-EEA subprocessors and prepare DPA addendum.

I'll CC security for a quick review of the freeze replication step.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Related links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-medigen-evidence

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@medigen.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-19T16:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: Delay to scheduled backups purge / legal hold

Ellen — thanks again and for the legal hold notice. Confirming Redwood's immediate plan and next steps: 

1) Implemented now: we have applied a tenant-level rollback_token and set snapshot freeze=true for Medigen. This prevents any automated purge workers from selecting or physically deleting snapshots.
2) Dry-run: Marissa will run a dry-run and provide a CSV of snapshot ids and a short narrative of which retention classes are affected (ETA 2 hours).
3) Subprocessor check: Karthik will suspend cross-border replication where subprocessors are non-EEA; this is precautionary and will be reversed only on express confirmation from Medigen Legal.
4) DPA addendum: Karthik will send a DocuSign link with language that references the rollback_token and the temporary suspension of replication (we will not require this for immediate 72-hour holds, but we will request it if the hold extends).

We will not perform any destructive purge actions for Medigen until we have explicit confirmation from your Legal team. We will also prepare the audit bundle (dry-run CSV, admin audit log, and a signed activity record) and share it in the secure drive link below.

Next checkpoint: we will reconvene at 2026-12-21T11:00 UTC unless Medigen Legal confirms earlier.

Link to evidence folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-medigen-evidence
DocuSign (DPA addendum) placeholder: https://app.redwood.com/docusign/placeholder-DELETION-REQ-9876

Kimberly Park
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
